headline: Azure agentless disk scanning drops from six custom RBAC roles to three; compliance authoring reworked
summary_md:
- **Microsoft Azure provider permissions** replaces the six ADS custom RBAC roles with three, confining every write and delete to the Cortex-created resource group.
- Three **compliance catalog** pages rewrite custom standard authoring: categories and controls are no longer built inside the standard wizard, and a control may now belong to more than one custom standard.
- The **Azure APIM** ingestion page drops a duplicated inbound policy snippet.
- The **Threat Management** landing page gains a link to an Extended Threat Intelligence section.
- A quiet day otherwise: six pages changed, nothing added or removed.

highlights.title: Agentless Disk Scanning is re-split into three Azure roles, with writes and deletes confined to one resource group
highlights.detail: ADSScannedAssetsRole, ADSOutpostRole and ADSEphemeralResourcesRole replace ADSConnectorDiskRole, ADSConnectorGalleryImageRole, ADSConnectorSnapshotRole, ADSConnectorVMRole and ADSGalleryImagesRole; only the ephemeral role can delete, and it is scoped to the Cortex-created resource group rather than the onboarded scope.

highlights.title: Terraform subscription onboarding names the outpost role without "Role"
highlights.detail: A new note states that Terraform subscription onboarding creates it as ADSOutpost-{suffix}, while Terraform management group onboarding and both ARM paths create ADSOutpostRole-{suffix}.

highlights.title: Custom standards no longer build their own categories and controls
highlights.detail: The Categories & Controls step becomes Select Controls, picking from existing controls or deferring via Create and Assign New Controls; the documented ceiling of 600 controls per standard goes with it.

highlights.title: A control can now be associated with more than one custom standard
highlights.detail: Both the create and edit metadata lists change from "a single custom standard" to one or more, and category and sub-category move to the top of the create form.

highlights.title: The Azure APIM inbound policy snippet was duplicated
highlights.detail: Three lines setting requestBody and requestHeaders appeared twice in the copy-paste block; the first copy is removed.

highlights.title: Threat Management links to an Extended Threat Intelligence section
highlights.detail: A content reference to threat-management/extended-threat-intelligence is inserted between Analytics and Threat Intel Management.

items.xsiam/configure-cortex-xsiam/cortex-xsia: ADSScannedAssetsRole, ADSOutpostRole and ADSEphemeralResourcesRole replace the six ADSConnector-era roles; every write and delete is now scoped to the Cortex-created resource group.
items.xsiam/cloud-security/monitor-and-track-c: Creating or editing a custom standard now ends in a Select Controls step; the inline Add Category, Add Subcategory and Add Control flow and the 600-control limit are gone.
A control can be associated with one or more custom standards rather than a single one, and the edit step now documents reassigning or creating categories and sub-categories.
Drops the RBAC and Pod security example and now states that controls are grouped into categories and sub-categories rather than that they can be.
items.xsiam/cloud-security/overview/secure-you: Removes a duplicated copy of the inbound policy snippet that set requestBody and requestHeaders twice.
items.xsiam/detect-investigate-and-respond-to-: Gains a content reference to a new Extended Threat Intelligence section alongside Analytics and Threat Intel Management.
